name: Allison Duck
bio: Allison Duck earned her Bachelor’s in English in 2005 and joined the Soil Food Web School as a Student Services Representative and Content Producer in 2019. Allison brings her past experiences as an EMT, freelance writer, director of public relations, technical editor, and grant writer to the Soil Food Web School. In addition, she helps students with their enrollment and content questions, contributes to content production, and supports the Marketing Department.

name: Alex Bright
bio: Alex is a Student Support Officer for the Soil Food Web School. With years of experience in IT and Customer Service, followed by a transition to the green arts, Alex brings a unique blend of technical expertise and a deep passion for sustainable practices. She graduated from the Royal Horticultural Society’s program in the UK, where she developed a strong foundation in horticulture. More recently, Alex completed a Diploma in Horticulture in Southern Ontario, further honing her knowledge of sustainable gardening practices and soil health. Alex has hands-on experience working at an organic vegetable farm and in large private gardens, which has deepened her understanding of soil management, plant care, and sustainable farming techniques. She is particularly passionate about the Soil Food Web approach and its potential to transform urban environments.

name: Dr. Caterina Capri
bio: Caterina Capri earned a Bachelor’s of Land and Agro-Forestry Sciences and then completed a Master’s degree in Food and Agricultural Technology specializing in Viticulture and Enology in Italy. She later did a PhD on herbaceous species selection to be used in Mediterranean vineyards based on water consumption, above-ground biomass and root characterization. Caterina has five research papers to her credit, the patent for a chamber to measure evapotranspiration and other empirical research studies. She has given presentations at conferences and held three webinars. Caterina loves nature and connecting the "pieces" together to work in an interdisciplinary way. Discovering Soil Food Web School for her felt like finding another piece of this puzzle called life. She works as a Soil Food Web Lab Technician and a Consultant Training Program instructor and mentor at the Soil Food Web School.

name: Dr. Nora Levay
bio: Nora Levay holds a master’s degree in agriculture with a specialization in pest control and a master’s degree in economics with a focus on finance. She earned her PhD in entomology, focusing her research on the dispersal patterns of the invasive insect pest Diabrotica virgifera virgifera LeConte in Europe. Nora has been involved in several international research collaborations and worked as a facilitator for a farmer field school as part of an FAO project, where she first learned about the participatory approach in knowledge transfer. After receiving a research scholarship, she spent six months at the Julius Kühn Institute in Germany. After transitioning from academia, Nora began consulting with farmers and served as a project manager for a German CRO, where she organized bird and small mammal field studies in Hungary. She also gained hands-on experience managing her own commercial orchard. Nora is a dedicated educator and science communicator, known for her ability to distill complex scientific concepts into accessible insights for those interested in the practical applications of academic knowledge.

name: Yolanda Hadjidemetriou
bio: Yolanda Hadjidemetriou joined the Soil Food Web School (SFWS) team in December 2025. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Film and TV Production and a Master’s in Acting for Stage and Screen. Yolanda began her career as a videographer, working with UCL, and later as a localization editor. Driven by a passion for sustainability, she joined SFWS to pursue a more eco-conscious path and began the Foundation Course at the Soil Food Web School, with the goal of growing and producing her own food. At SFWS, Yolanda specializes in videography and editing for social media and various digital platforms, helping to create engaging content that promotes regenerative farming practices.

name: Anna Depetris
bio: Anna Depetris is a dedicated microbiologist with a foundation in freshwater ecosystems, now expanding her focus to soil science and regenerative agriculture. She is committed to making a meaningful contribution to the transition toward sustainable development and is eager to support other students in exploring the Soil Food Web approach.

name: Laura Campos
bio: Laura Campos completed her Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Biology at the University of Costa Rica. Her Master’s scores were the highest of all graduates at the college when she graduated. As a specialist in Pests and Diseases, Laura brings professional experience in breeding coffee borers at the Center of Research in Cellular and Molecular Biology and being an Instructor for General Zoology and Zoology for Health Science at the University of Costa Rica. Laura began in Content Development with SFWS but was promoted to CLP and CTP Instructor position when she completed Tier 3 Professional Development with the SFWS school. However, Laura continues working with Dr. Godschalx on an entire Pest and Diseases program for the SFWS students. In fact, Laura’s research, "Virulence of native isolates of entomopathogenic fungi (Hypocreales) against the ’sweetpotato whitefly’" was recently published in the Journal of Invertebrate Pathology.

name: Dr. Elina Psara
bio: Elina holds a Ph.D. from Ulster University, focusing on nutrition’s impact on human health. She also has an MSc from Imperial College London and a BSc from the University of Birmingham, all in human biology-related fields. During her doctoral studies, Elina recognized the importance of all trophic levels in the food chain for human health, ultimately leading to an understanding of the crucial importance of soil health. She discovered the Soil Food Web approach, and its ability to cost-effectively regenerate soils. Now part of the Soil Food Web family, Elina guides students with the goal of enhancing soils and ecosystems globally. She’s enthusiastic about conducting further research into the connection between soil health and human health through nutrient density.

name: Tommy Tapper
bio: I sometimes think I took the most roundabout way to get to where I am today, a proud and enthusiastic employee of the Soil Food Web School. At university, I studied Sociology and Communication. It wasn’t until after college, working at an organic vegetable and chicken farm in Rhode Island, USA that I started realizing that growing food was the greatest thing in the world. But shortly after, I developed another passion, teaching middle school students. I instantly wanted to find a way to pursue both passions, but the recurring mental picture of 12-year-olds running around with pitchforks terrified me. After ten-plus years of teaching middle school, being a part of various community gardens, and growing food wherever I lived, I have found that magical place where both passions coexist. I continue to be amazed by the opportunity to work with so many inspiring students and fellow mentors all around the world.

name: Dr. Kathleen Groppe
bio: Dr. Kathleen Groppe is a molecular ecologist, regenerative rancher, and educator whose work bridges soil biology, ecology, and agricultural systems. She holds a Ph.D. in Molecular Ecology from the Universität Basel in Switzerland and earned both Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Cell and Molecular Biology from the University of California, Santa Barbara, where she conducted research on the genes involved in avocado ripening. Kathleen grew up on a small avocado ranch near San Diego, California where she raised a pig for Future Farmers of America (FFA). Her father was an ornithologist (who spent his career restoring the peregrine falcon, an endangered species, to the wild), her step-father was an entomologist (who studied the evolution of the tsetse fly over continents), and her mother was, and is, a master gardener and long-time volunteer at the San Diego Museum of Natural History. Kathleen’s scientific background includes research in molecular biology, medical diagnostics, and microbial ecology. Over time, her interests shifted increasingly toward soil ecology, plant–microbe interactions, ecosystem restoration, and regenerative land management. Dr. Groppe owns and manages a regenerative cattle ranch in North Texas that has undergone extensive prairie and wetland restoration. Her work on the ranch has included observational and applied studies examining soil structure, biodiversity, hydrology, and the effects of management practices on ecological recovery and resilience. In addition to her scientific and agricultural work, Dr. Groppe was a homeschool teacher for 13 years, and is a longtime artisan jeweler and small business owner whose work reflects a deep connection to natural systems and landscape.
